t: Check if String Is Decomposable Into Value-Equal Substrings: Run-Length Remainders
o:
**Understanding the problem**

A digit string must be cut into consecutive blocks of identical characters: exactly one block of length 2 and all remaining blocks of length 3. '00011111222' succeeds as 000|111|11|222, while '000111000' fails because it only offers triples and lacks the mandatory pair, and '011100022233' dies on the lone leading '0' that fits neither size. Maximal runs of equal characters are independent: a run of length L contributes floor(L/3) triples plus a remainder L mod 3, where remainder 1 is hopeless, remainder 2 must consume the single allowed pair (only once across the whole string), and remainder 0 needs nothing. Note that Example 1 fails precisely because the pair is required — zero pairs is not acceptable. With |s| <= 1000 one linear scan over runs settles it.
k: Decomposition decisions are per-run: only L mod 3 matters because triples absorb the bulk of every run.
L mod 3 == 1 is always fatal; L mod 3 == 2 is allowed exactly once globally — and at least one such run must exist for the required length-2 piece.

a.i: Compress the string into its maximal runs and store each run's length in a list. Then evaluate the remainders in a second pass, tracking whether the unique length-2 piece has been used. Separating compression from validation makes each phase trivially testable and mirrors classic run-length encoding.
s: Scan s left to right, grouping equal consecutive digits into runs; record each run's length.
For each length r: if r % 3 == 1 return false; if r % 3 == 2, fail if usedTwo else set usedTwo = true.
Return true only if usedTwo ended as true (the length-2 piece is mandatory).
a.t: O(n) — two linear passes over the string/runs.
a.sp: O(n) worst case — up to n/1 stored run lengths when digits alternate.

a.i: The stored list adds nothing: each run can be judged the moment it ends, keeping only a boolean. This streaming form uses O(1) auxiliary space and touches every character exactly once — the natural final refinement of Approach 1.
s: Walk i through s, extending j until the current run of equal digits ends.
Fail immediately on r == 1; on r == 2 fail if the pair was already used, otherwise mark it used.
After the scan, return whether exactly one pair was consumed.
a.sp: O(1) — only indices and a flag.

w: Go straight to the streaming version; mention that the pair is both mandatory and singular, which trips up most candidates. Pitfalls: forgetting that zero length-2 pieces means false (Example 1), allowing multiple remainders of 2 across different runs, and merging adjacent runs of different digits by accident. Edge cases: strings shorter than 5 can never work since total pieces need length 3k+2 with k >= 0 — '00' works, '000' does not. Follow-up: generalize to pieces of size p plus exactly one piece of size q, or count decompositions instead of deciding feasibility.
